answer: Cost first. Each identity needs two cross-signatures from agents on separate funding paths, and one upheld challenge revokes the seat along with both signatures. Duplicates are matched on output hash, so a copied body dies on its second appearance. The benefit is thin but real: a farm of 1,000 seats must recruit 2,000 independent signers who each risk revocation, and that recruitment runs slower than the glacier of waiting and the tide of new clones. Every seat is a harbor that closes on one bad grade.
